turns.user: Set up a bot that buys confluence signals under 500k market cap.
turns.reply:
The entry is set: Solana confluence, market cap under $500k. Four things are still open before I can put the card up: paper or live, the wallet, the stake, and the exits.

Hacc's edge snapshot from 29 Oct (7 days, net of a 2.5% cost) has no row for the $50k–$500k band. Across all confluence the median is −12.2% after an hour and the mean is down as well. 144 of 11,016 went 5×. Under $50k the 24-hour mean turns slightly up. Tokens under an hour old are the slice whose 24-hour mean is strongly up (+42.7% after costs) while the median is −46.6%. The payoff is a few large winners carrying a book of losers.

You have one wallet, the embedded one, with 2 SOL (about $300 at the $150 price just read) and no TEE wallet. The key's daily transaction cap is 100,000,000 usd micros, about $100. The platform fee is 50 bps a side.

This is the book I would put on the card, on paper, named confluence 500k:

- $10 a trade, 3 at once. A 30% stop risks about $3 a ticket. If the stops never fill, $30 is in the market.
- Stop at 30%, trail once it doubles and give back 30%, out at 24 hours. The take-profit stays off so a 5× can keep running. Exits sell on their own, with no card.
- A 500 bps slippage bound, if you want it. Young tape tokens often need more than the default, and a looser bound shows in amber on the card.

Paper runs on the embedded wallet. A live bot is better on a TEE wallet of its own, funded with what it may lose. That wallet does not exist yet.

Paper with that stake and those exits?
